text: His wife. <break time="0.8s" /> Who was in despair. <break time="0.8s" /> Came to the prison. <break time="0.8s" /> With their small children. <break time="0.8s" /> And when she saw him. <break time="0.8s" /> In chains among criminals. <break time="0.8s" /> She fainted. <break time="0.8s" /> She told him. <break time="0.8s" /> That her petition to the Czar had been refused. <break time="0.8s" /> And she reminded him sadly. <break time="0.8s" /> Of her dream about his gray hair. <break time="0.8s" /> Then running her fingers through his hair. <break time="0.8s" /> She said. <break time="0.8s" /> Vanya dearest, tell your wife the truth. <break time="0.8s" /> Was it not you who did it. <break time="0.8s" /> So you, too, suspect me. <break time="0.8s" /> Cried Aksionov. <break time="0.8s" /> And hiding his face in his hands. <break time="0.8s" /> He began to weep. <break time="0.8s" /> When his family had gone for the last time. <break time="0.8s" /> He thought. <break time="0.8s" /> Only God can know the truth. <break time="0.8s" /> And only from Him can I expect mercy. <break time="0.8s" /> He wrote no more petitions. <break time="0.8s" /> And only prayed to God. <break time="0.8s" /> And he was later whipped. <break time="0.8s" /> And sent to Siberia. <break time="0.8s" /> With other prisoners. <break time="0.8s" /> Twenty six years passed in Siberia. <break time="0.8s" /> His hair turning as white as snow. <break time="0.8s" /> And his beard growing long, thin, and gray. <break time="0.8s" /> All his cheerfulness was gone. <break time="0.8s" /> And he walked slowly. <break time="0.8s" /> With a stooped back. <break time="0.8s" /> Spoke little. <break time="0.8s" /> Never laughed. <break time="0.8s" /> And often prayed. <break time="0.8s" /> He learned to make boots in prison. <break time="0.8s" /> And the other prisoners. <break time="0.8s" /> Who respected his gentleness. <break time="0.8s" /> Called him Grandfather and the Saint.
